title: Common Skin Problems in Children: When Should Parents Visit a Dermatologist?

alt: Common skin problems in children, featuring a baby with a facial rash
intro: A new rash, persistent itching or a patch of dry skin can leave parents wondering whether home care is enough. Children's skin concerns often look similar, yet have different causes. Watching how a rash changes, how your child feels and whether sleep or feeding is affected can help you decide when to seek advice. A Pediatric Dermatologist in Pune can assess recurring or unclear symptoms and recommend care suited to your child's age.
sections: Common Skin Problems Seen in Children

Common concerns include eczema, heat rash, irritation in the nappy area, contact dermatitis, warts and fungal infections. Babies may develop cradle cap, while older children can experience acne. Not every bump needs treatment, but the appearance alone cannot reliably identify the cause.

Note when the problem started, whether anyone else at home is itchy and whether a new soap, detergent or medicine was introduced. Photographs taken as symptoms change can help during the consultation.
Eczema, Rashes and Skin Allergies

Eczema often causes dry, itchy patches that come and go. Contact dermatitis can follow exposure to an irritating or allergenic substance. Heat and sweating may also trigger discomfort. A rash does not automatically mean a food allergy, and removing foods without medical guidance can affect a child's nutrition.

Use gentle, fragrance-free products, avoid vigorous scrubbing and keep nails short. For dry skin, a suitable moisturiser may help. Ask a clinician before applying medicated creams, particularly on a baby's face or under a nappy. Avoid sharing another family member's prescription.
Skin Infections and Other Warning Signs

Increasing warmth, tenderness, pus, crusting or a rapidly spreading rash may suggest infection. Scalp scaling with patchy hair loss also deserves assessment. Some infections spread through close contact or shared personal items, so avoid sharing towels and combs while seeking advice.

Seek prompt medical care when a rash accompanies fever or your child seems unwell. Breathing difficulty, sudden lip or tongue swelling, marked drowsiness or a purple rash that does not fade under pressure require emergency assessment. Do not wait for a routine skin appointment.
When Should Parents Consult a Dermatologist?

Arrange a consultation for a rash that persists, keeps returning, spreads or interferes with sleep, school or play. Painful skin, unexplained blisters, changing birthmarks and symptoms that worsen despite prescribed care also warrant review. Babies and children with reduced immunity may need earlier assessment.

A paediatrician can assess general illness and coordinate specialist care. Dermatology review is particularly helpful when the diagnosis remains unclear or ongoing treatment needs adjustment. Avoid repeated trials of steroid-antifungal combination creams without a diagnosis.
How a Pediatric Skin Consultation Helps

The dermatologist reviews symptoms, family history, previous treatments and possible triggers, then examines the affected skin. Tests such as a skin scraping or allergy assessment are considered only when clinically appropriate. Many childhood skin concerns can be assessed without extensive testing.

Parents should receive clear instructions about where and how long to use medicines, everyday skin care and when to return. Bring current prescriptions and product names. Ask about SkinCity's Baby Skin Clinic for age-appropriate evaluation and follow-up.
Frequently Asked Questions

Is every childhood rash contagious?

No. Eczema and irritation are not contagious, while some infections can spread. An examination helps distinguish them.

Should I stop milk or other foods for eczema?

Do not restrict foods without medical advice. Allergy investigation depends on symptoms and clinical history.

Can adult skin creams be used on babies?

Not automatically. Ingredients, strength and application area matter; check with your child's clinician first.

What should I bring to the appointment?

Bring photographs, medication details and a brief timeline, including any fever, new products or affected household members.

title: Microscopic Hair Analysis: How Dermatologists Identify the Root Cause of Hair Loss
seoTitle: Microscopic Hair Analysis in Pune | Hair Loss Diagnosis
description: Discover how microscopic hair analysis helps dermatologists examine scalp health, hair follicles, and possible causes of hair loss.
alt: Microscopic hair analysis using a magnifying device to examine the scalp
intro: Finding more hair on your pillow or noticing a widening parting can be unsettling. Hair loss has many possible causes, and choosing treatment without an assessment may delay appropriate care. Microscopic Hair Analysis in Pune can give dermatologists a closer view of hair and scalp features. These findings support a diagnosis alongside your symptoms and medical history; the examination cannot identify every cause of hair loss on its own.
sections: What Is Microscopic Hair Analysis?

The term describes close examination of hair or scalp using magnification. Trichoscopy uses a handheld dermatoscope or digital device to inspect the scalp surface, hair shafts and follicular openings. In selected cases, collected hairs may be examined under a microscope for structural changes.

These methods answer different questions. A surface examination cannot directly show every structure beneath the skin or establish a nutritional deficiency. Ask which examination is proposed and what information it can realistically provide.
How Does a Dermatologist Examine Hair and Scalp Health?

The consultation begins with questions about onset, shedding, family history, recent illness, childbirth, medicines, diet and hair-care practices. The doctor examines the distribution of thinning and checks for scaling, inflammation or scarring. A gentle hair-pull test may be appropriate.

Magnified examination then helps compare affected areas with other parts of the scalp. Images may be recorded with consent for future comparison. Tell the clinic about recent colouring, scalp products and treatments, and follow its preparation instructions rather than stopping prescribed medicines yourself.
What Can Microscopic Hair Analysis Reveal?

Magnification can highlight differences in hair thickness, broken hairs, scaling and changes around follicular openings. Particular patterns can support possibilities such as patterned hair loss, alopecia areata or inflammatory scalp disease. Examination of a hair shaft may also help explain unusual breakage.

Similar findings can occur in different conditions, and more than one cause may coexist. Microscopy does not measure hormone levels or reliably diagnose vitamin deficiencies. Blood tests, fungal testing or a scalp biopsy may be recommended when the history and examination suggest a need.
Who May Benefit from This Examination?

People with persistent shedding, widening partings, a receding hairline, patchy loss or unexplained breakage may benefit from closer assessment. Scalp itching, tenderness, redness or scaling can provide additional reasons to consult a dermatologist. Sudden hair loss or painful inflamed patches should be assessed promptly.

Not everyone needs every test. The dermatologist selects examinations according to the suspected condition. Bring a list of medicines and supplements, previous results and older photographs showing your usual hair density, if available.
How the Findings Help Guide Treatment Planning

The findings help distinguish problems involving shedding, shaft breakage, follicular changes or scalp inflammation. Your clinician combines these clues with the consultation before discussing options. Depending on the diagnosis, care may involve observation, changes to hair practices, prescribed medicine or further investigations.

There is no single treatment for all hair loss. Supplements and procedures are not automatically needed after a scan. Follow-up photographs can help track change over time, but outcomes and timelines vary. SkinCity's Microscopic Hair Analysis service explains the available assessment approach.
Frequently Asked Questions

Is a magnified scalp examination painful?

Surface trichoscopy is generally non-invasive. Hair sampling or a biopsy is different and should be explained separately if recommended.

Will it reveal the exact cause immediately?

Sometimes findings strongly support a diagnosis. Other cases need additional history, tests or follow-up before the cause becomes clear.

Can it predict guaranteed hair regrowth?

No. Examination helps assessment and planning; it cannot guarantee a treatment response or a specific amount of regrowth.

Do I need blood tests as well?

Only when clinically indicated. Your symptoms and examination guide which tests, if any, are useful.
Consult a Hair Specialist in Pune

If shedding or scalp changes persist, arrange a dermatology consultation at SkinCity India in Pune. Ask what the examination shows, what remains uncertain and how follow-up will be measured. A clear diagnosis and realistic discussion can help you make informed decisions about your hair care.
